summary: Fitzedward Hall was an Indologist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (~1840–1842) and Harvard University (~1842–1846). He later held a post at King's College London from circa 1862 to 1869.

Flavio A. Geisshuesler works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the universities of Bern, Lausanne, and Virginia (PhD), supervised by David Germano, and held a postdoctoral research post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem under Dan Martin in 2019.

Florin Deleanu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg (PhD under Lambert Schmithausen). His appointments include professorships at Kansai Medical University (~1999–2002) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2002).
Florinda De Simini is an Indologist. She held an attested post at the University of Naples Federico II in 2016 and a post at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" circa 2017.

Francesco Sferra is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Raffaele Torella. He has held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2002), University of Naples Federico II (attested 2010), IsIAO (attested 2015), and Series Minor (attested 2020).

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1779–1783), served in the Indian Medical Service (~1794–1815), and succeeded Henry Thomas Colebrooke.

Francis Gladwin was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. A founding member of the Asiatic Society (~1784–1812), he served as professor of Persian at Fort William College from circa 1801 to 1805.

Francis H. Cook is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He served as professor (~1970–1989) and emeritus professor (~1989) at UC Riverside, and chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research in 1999.

Francis N. J. is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Attested in 2002, he earned a Master's in Ancient History at the University of Calicut and completed doctoral studies supervised by M. R. Raghava Varier.
Francis Robinson is a historian and scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Bexhill College (~1956–1963) and became a professor at Royal Holloway, University of London, circa 1973.

Francis Tiso is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed studies at Cornell University (~1968–1972), Harvard Divinity School (~1972–1975), and Columbia University (~1982–1989).

Francis Woodman Cleaves was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, sinology, and linguistics. He studied at Harvard University (~1933–1942) and later held an academic post there from circa 1946 to 1980.

Francis X. Clooney specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Fordham and the University of Chicago (doctorate ~1984), he held posts at Boston College, University of Oxford, Harvard University, and the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies.

Francisco García Ayuso was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under Martin Haug between circa 1868 and 1871.

Francisco Varela worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile, University of Chile, and Harvard, he co-founded the Mind & Life Institute and held posts at the University of Chile, Naropa University, and CNRS.

Franciscus Verellen is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and history. Educated at Hamburg, Oxford, and EPHE under Kristofer Schipper, he has held posts at the EFEO (director 2004–2014), Princeton, IAS, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaii under teachers including Eliot Deutsch and David J. Kalupahana, and completed his doctorate under Stewart Sutherland.

Frank Raymond Allchin was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at the University of London (~1946–1954), he held positions at SOAS, the University of Cambridge (~1954–1989), and the Ancient India and Iran Trust (~1978–2010).

Frank-Richard Hamm was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring, later teaching at Hamburg (~1954–1964) before becoming Professor of Indology at the University of Bonn in 1965.

Franklin Edgerton was an Indologist and linguist. After studying at Cornell, Munich, Jena, and Johns Hopkins (PhD under Maurice Bloomfield), he served as professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Salisbury Professor at Yale University (1926, 1946).
